metadata.case_name: LEE NGA LAI v. KONG MAN PUI AND OTHERS

plaintiff.education_level: Primary two student at the time of the accident

injuries.description: Fracture of both right tibia and fibula
source: X-ray showed that both her right tibia and fibula were fractured.

injuries.description: Open wound of right tibia exposing underlying bone
source: There was an open wound of 3cm exposing the underlying bone at her right tibia.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of lower leg

injuries.description: Facial soft tissue injuries including lacerations and abrasion (below right ear, chin, right face) with bruising at right infra-orbital area/right eyelid
injuries.body_part: face (including below right ear, chin, right infra-orbital area/right eyelid)
source: The Plaintiff also suffered facial injuries, including a 3cm laceration wound below the right ear, a 1cm laceration on the chin, abrasion with swelling on her right face, and bruise and swelling at the right infra-orbital area or right eyelid.

injuries.description: Right eye and orbital soft tissue injury
source: Dr Poon Kai Ming added that the right eye and orbital soft tissue injury healed with no complaint or any recognisable scar.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of eyeball or orbital tissues

injuries.description: Permanent scarring including faint fine pale horizontal linear scar at right ear lobe, raised hypertrophic scar behind and below ear lobe, multiple scars on right lower leg including a noticeable slightly pigmented raised thickened scar
injuries.body_part: right ear lobe; area behind and below right ear; right lower leg
source: Dr Otto Au and Dr Ian Nicholson, the Plaintiffs and the 1st and 2nd Defendants respective plastic surgery specialist, noted the Plaintiff had the following scars :
(a) right ear lobe : faint fine pale horizontal linear scar measuring 10x1mm causing a small notch at the rim;
(b) neck behind and below the ear lobe : noticeable raised thickened resolving hypertrophic scar measuring 25x8mm that was partially concealed by the lobule and the lie of the Plaintiffs hair;

(c) right lower leg : Dr Au said there were about 15 scars of various sizes distributed along the anterior and lateral surface of the leg with the largest (55x20mm) on the dorsal surface of the junction between the lower leg and foot. Dr Nicholson agreed there were 2 pale flat areas of scars (22x10mm and 30x10mm) on the anterior and lateral aspect of the lower right leg as well as multiple faintly hypertrophic puncture scars where the external fixators were inserted. He said there was a noticeable ugly scar that was slightly pigmented as well as raised and thickened. Both experts agreed it was mildly hypertrophic.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the knee or lower leg

manifestations.description: Pain at her right leg and right eye on admission
Open wound exposing underlying bone at right tibia
Hypertrophic and other permanent scars (cosmetic disability)
Wore pressure garments for about 4 months
Able to walk normally by 27th June 2002

treatments_received: Emergency operation to clean the leg wound and fix the tibial fracture with an external fixator
Ring external fixator applied to immobilise the tibial fracture
Removal of the ring fixator (readmitted in April 2002) and brace given
Pressure garment therapy for about 4 months
Gel applied to the scar on the right ear
treatments_future: Dr Otto Au recommended possible laser treatment, injection to the ankle scar and surgery to correct ear lobe notching and neck scar (not adopted by the court as appropriate)
Dr Nicholson mentioned intralesional cortisone injection as a possible treatment (not adopted by the court as appropriate)

losses.description: Permanent cosmetic disability from scars (ear lobe notch; hypertrophic scar behind/below ear; multiple scars on right lower leg) causing concealment of the right leg scar when swimming and some potential embarrassment; judged to be permanent though not highly conspicuous.
Possible restriction from certain careers (for example modelling or professions requiring exposure of the foot) because of cosmetic effects of scars.

comparable_cases.case_name: Ho Tze Ho (an infant suing by his mother and next friend Chin Shui Ying) v Chui Chung Wah and anor
comparable_cases.injury_description: Closed fracture of the left tibia and fibula with multiple abrasions on both knees, left leg, left forefoot, lip and chin; debridement of the leg and foot wounds and close reduction of the fracture with long leg dynacast; conspicuous, thickened, hyperpigmented and hypertrophic scars on left foot
